oracle.encoding: one little-endian uint16 per case, in the order of decision_space.chunks() and, within a chunk, decision_space_dt3.iter_chunk() (the dt-2 order with bc = False, then with bc = True); the value indexes dt3_decisions.json 'decisions'

BC_DETERMINISM.statement: deciding an equal bc case built from fresh objects gives an identical decision

BC_EFFECT.statement: where bc changes a decision, the result is D-13a UNRESOLVED_IDENTITY, status uncertain, value null, disposition ABSTAIN, carrying BIBLIOGRAPHIC_OBJECT_CONFLICT and exactly the twin's pair reasons

BC_EVERY_POSITIVE_BLOCKED.statement: every dt-2 D-14 positive becomes D-13a under bc

BC_NO_NOTICE_OR_NOT_FOUND.statement: bc never yields NOTICE_CITED or NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SOURCES that the twin lacks

BC_NO_POSITIVE.statement: a case with bc whose deciding lookup is matched never yields a positive finding

BC_ONLY_REMOVES_POSITIVES.statement: bc changes a decision only where the dt-2 twin is a D-14 positive (it never creates or moves any other decision: D-1 to D-13 and D-15 to D-17 keep their place, class and reasons)

BC_REASON_IFF.statement: BIBLIOGRAPHIC_OBJECT_CONFLICT is a reason exactly when bc holds and the rule is D-13a

BC_TOTAL.statement: every bc = True case is decided by exactly one rule of dt-3

EQUIVALENCE_BC_FALSE.statement: with bc = False, the dt-3 decision is the dt-2 oracle's decision for the same case
